sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018, then recovered 17.1% in FY2021 [D42][D93][D246].
The FY2017 decline came with refranchising of bottling operations, which cut operating cash flow by 20% [P75].
Operating margin bottomed at 20.7% in FY2016 and peaked at 28.7% in FY2025, a 7.5pp jump in the latest year [F41][F50][D463].
That FY2025 jump was driven by lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement, plus concentrate volume growth and pricing [P12].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of growth, while finished product operations added 0.3pp [D532][D534][D541].
Non-US concentrate operations contributed 1.3pp of FY2025 growth, but non-US finished product operations subtracted 1.0pp [D548][D555].
North America was the largest segment at 40.9% of FY2025 revenue, contributing 1.5pp of growth [D611][D613].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025 while unit case volume was even [P16].
Operating income grew 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth in FY2025, and net income grew 23.3% while diluted EPS grew 23.6% [D450][D449][D451][D453].
FY2025 operating margin of 28.7% sits above the 26.0% window median and at the window high [F50][D766][D765].
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6%, against a 60.7% window median [F30][D462][D772].
The gross margin gain came from favorable pricing and prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and higher commodity costs [P14].
In the FY2025 bridge, cost of revenue added 0.6pp, SG&A added 0.7pp and other lines added 6.2pp to operating margin [D475][D476][D477].
SG&A fell 0.4% on lower Foundation contributions and incentive expense, partly offset by severance and higher advertising [P13][D466].
Net margin of 27.3% trailed operating margin by 1.4pp, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [F70][D810][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion was only 0.57x net income in FY2025, the window low against a 1.18x median [F100][D436][D799][D800].
Free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x net income, also the window low, and an 11.0% margin against a 20.2% median [F120][D437][D776][D433][D775].
FY2025 operating cash flow rose 9% on strong cash operating results, lower tax payments and working-capital timing [P1].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F110][D432][D438].
Cash and equivalents were $10.3 billion at FY2025, down 5.2%, and the current ratio rose to 1.46x, the window high [F160][D458][F200][D780].
Net debt is not measurable for FY2025 because long-term debt stops at FY2023, so the net-cash peer rank cannot be used [X194][R9].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D444][D445].
Dividends of $8.8 billion dwarfed $746 million of buybacks, and the diluted share count fell only 0.2% [X145][X135][D468].
Return on average equity of 46.0% ranked at the 67th percentile against six staples peers, whose median was 36.5% [D448][D797][D798].

Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported, so growth across those years mixes presentations [F2][X2][F3][X3][R1].
Long-term debt is missing after FY2023, so total debt, net cash and the net-cash peer rank are unavailable for FY2024 and FY2025 [X194][R9].
Cash and investments omit an unmapped short-term investment line, understating the total by $3.6 billion in FY2025 [F160][D440][R11].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 214.2% in FY2024 [D344][D395][D445][R2].
Free cash flow fell below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [D387][D437][R3].
If FY2026 operating margin falls back below the 26.0% window median, the FY2025 charge-driven gain would look one-off [D766].
If operating cash flow to net income stays below the 1.18x window median, the weak conversion of FY2024 and FY2025 would look structural [D800].
If buybacks plus dividends stay above 100% of free cash flow, the FY2025 level of 179.9% would keep pressuring the balance sheet [D445].
